findings.description: storage_encrypted is explicitly set to false, so the RDS MySQL volumes, automated snapshots and logs are stored unencrypted. Any data in this database, including the EMPLOYEES PII table created by the app, is written to disk in cleartext.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the RDS instance a public endpoint reachable from outside the VPC, removing the network boundary around the database and exposing MySQL to internet-based credential attacks. The instance is also unencrypted and uses the predictable 'admin' master user.
The master username is hard-coded to 'admin', a well-known default that removes any uncertainty for an attacker brute-forcing the publicly accessible endpoint.

The RDS master username and var.password are interpolated directly into the instance user_data script and written to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user data is retrievable in cleartext by anyone with instance metadata access or ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute, leaking the database master password.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*". Attached via an instance profile to an internet-facing web server, a single application compromise yields full read/write control of all S3 data, all EC2 infrastructure and all RDS databases in the account, including privilege-escalation paths such as launching instances with other roles or modifying DB master passwords.

No metadata_options block is specified, so instance metadata service v1 remains enabled. Combined with a PHP application taking unvalidated POST input and a wildcard s3/ec2/rds instance role, an SSRF or RCE in the web app allows trivial theft of the role's temporary credentials.

No root_block_device or ebs_block_device encryption is configured, so the instance volume — which stores the database password in /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc — is left unencrypted at rest unless account-level default encryption happens to be on.

The user_data provisions only httpd on port 80 with no TLS configuration or termination layer, so the form submitting employee names and addresses and the resulting query output traverse the network in cleartext.

The parameter group sets only character set parameters and does not set require_secure_transport = 1, and the PHP client calls mysqli_connect with no TLS options. Traffic to a publicly accessible MySQL endpoint can therefore occur unencrypted.

Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the RDS security group, providing an unrestricted outbound path that aids data exfiltration and command-and-control if the database host is compromised.

The lifecycle ignore_changes on password combined with passing var.password into instance user data and exporting the endpoint means the database credential material is managed outside of a secrets manager; the password value will also be persisted in cleartext in Terraform state.
